content.text:
## Current state of the code

rb_insert ([src/rbtree.c:47-99](src/rbtree.c#L47-L99)) only does the BST half of the algorithm right now. It walks down with `cur`/`parent` exactly like `rb_find`, links the new node `n` in as `RB_RED`, and stops — the fixup call is a literal `TODO` at [src/rbtree.c:83-84](src/rbtree.c#L83-L84):

```c
n->color  = RB_RED;
/* TODO: red-black fixup. A fresh non-root node inserted red can now
 * have a red parent, which rb_validate will reject until fixup lands. */
```

So right now every inserted node is red, including the root, which is why [tests/test_rbtree.c:844](tests/test_rbtree.c#L844) (`test_rb_insert_bst_only`) exists as a separate, fixup-independent suite that checks shape/color with plain `assert()` instead of `rb_validate`. The fixup-dependent cases (5, 7–11) already call `rb_validate` and will fail until fixup lands.

## What the fixup needs to restore

After a plain BST insert of a red leaf `n`, three of the four invariants `rb_validate` checks still hold automatically; only one can break:
- BST ordering — untouched by insert.
- Equal black-height on all paths ([src/rbtree.c:158-159](src/rbtree.c#L158-L159)) — untouched, since `n` is red and contributes 0 to black-height.
- Root is black ([src/rbtree.c:167-168](src/rbtree.c#L167-L168)) — can break only if `n` *is* the root (first insert into an empty tree).
- No red node has a red child ([src/rbtree.c:149-151](src/rbtree.c#L149-L151)) — this is the one that breaks: if `n->parent` is red, you now have red-red.

Fixup's whole job is to walk up from `n` clearing red-red violations without disturbing black-height, then force the root black as a final catch-all.

## The fixup loop (CLRS-style, mapped to this struct)

```
z = n
while z->parent->color == RB_RED:
    if z->parent == z->parent->parent->left:
        y = z->parent->parent->right      # uncle
        if y->color == RB_RED:
            # Case 1
            z->parent->color = BLACK
            y->color = BLACK
            z->parent->parent->color = RED
            z = z->parent->parent
        else:
            if z == z->parent->right:
                # Case 2
                z = z->parent
                rotate_left(t, z)
            # Case 3
            z->parent->color = BLACK
            z->parent->parent->color = RED
            rotate_right(t, z->parent->parent)
    else:
        (mirror image, swap left/right)
t->root->color = BLACK
```

Because `t->nil` is a real sentinel node whose `left`/`right`/`parent` all point to itself ([src/rbtree.c:34](src/rbtree.c#L34)), `z->parent->parent` and `y` are always safe to dereference without extra null checks — that's the whole reason the design uses a sentinel instead of `NULL`.

The loop only ever runs when `z->parent` is red, which by invariant means `z->parent` isn't the root (root is always black), so `z->parent->parent` is guaranteed to exist and be black.

## The three cases (plus the mirror)

**Case 1 — uncle is red.** Both parent and uncle can be pushed black, grandparent turns red to preserve black-height, and the violation (now possibly red-red between grandparent and *its* parent) is pushed two levels up. This is a pure recolor, no rotation, and it's why the loop continues with `z = grandparent`.

**Case 2 — uncle is black, `z` is an "inner" child (triangle).** `z` and its parent are on opposite sides (e.g. parent is a left child, `z` is `parent`'s *right* child). One rotation at `parent` converts this into Case 3's shape — it doesn't fix anything by itself, it just falls through immediately.

**Case 3 — uncle is black, `z` is an "outer" child (line).** Parent and `z` are on the same side. Recolor parent black / grandparent red, then rotate at the grandparent. This terminates the loop — no further violation is introduced, since the rotation's new subtree root (parent) is now black.

The `else` branch mirrors all three with left/right swapped (uncle is `parent->parent->left`, rotations are right/left instead of left/right).

**Final step:** `t->root->color = BLACK` unconditionally. This is required even when the loop never executes — e.g. inserting into an empty tree makes `n` the root, red, with no parent to trigger the loop at all.

## How the test cases exercise each case

- **Case 7, ascending run `a..g`** ([tests/test_rbtree.c:588](tests/test_rbtree.c#L588)): each new key lands as a right child of the previous rightmost node — that's the RR "line" shape, i.e. repeated Case 3 with left-rotations at the grandparent. Matches the comment "forces left-rotations."
- **Case 8, descending run `g..a`** ([tests/test_rbtree.c:627](tests/test_rbtree.c#L627)): mirror — LL line shape, repeated Case 3 with right-rotations.
- **Case 9, LR zigzag `c,a,b`** ([tests/test_rbtree.c:661-666](tests/test_rbtree.c#L661-L666)): `a` inserts red under root `c`, loop doesn't run (`a`'s parent `c` is black). `b` inserts red as `a`'s *right* child — `a` is `c`'s left child, so `b` is an inner grandchild → Case 2 (rotate left at `a`) falling through to Case 3 (rotate right at `c`), a genuine double rotation.
- **Case 10, RL zigzag `a,c,b`** ([tests/test_rbtree.c:698-701](tests/test_rbtree.c#L698-L701)): exact mirror of Case 9.
- **Case 11, mixed order** ([tests/test_rbtree.c:730-745](tests/test_rbtree.c#L730-L745)): 11 keys inserted in an order designed to hit Case 1 recolors and rotations on both sides, not just one shape repeated.

Since insert uses parent pointers (not a recursive top-down insert), the fixup will also need `rotate_left`/`rotate_right` helpers that correctly relink `parent` pointers on both sides of the rotation (including the moved subtree's child and the grandparent-side link into `t->root` when the rotation happens at the root) — that plumbing doesn't exist in the file yet either.
The fixup logic looks good. Draft rotate_left and rotate_right and put them above rb_insert in your draft script. Don't edit anything.

# Update tests/test_rbtree.c to reflect landed insert-fixup

## Context

`rb_insert` in `src/rbtree.c` now implements full red-black fixup (rotations
+ recoloring) after a prior review found and fixed two bugs: a missing
node-linkage step, and a broken mirror-side Case 3 (wrong node recolored,
wrong color on the grandparent, wrong rotation direction). With fixup
landed, `tests/test_rbtree.c` needs to catch up:

- `test_rb_insert_bst_only` was explicitly documented as a temporary
  milestone checkpoint for *pre-fixup* behavior (its own header comment says
  so). One of its three sub-cases now asserts something fixup directly
  contradicts (a degenerate right-leaning chain with no rebalancing); this
  is deleted, not weakened, per CLAUDE.md's "never weaken a test" rule --
  the code correctly changed out from under the test's premise, and the gap
  was flagged as temporary from the start.
- Two more minimal structural cases (LL and RR straight-line rotations) are
  added alongside the existing LR/RL zigzag cases, rounding out all four
  fixup shapes with exact 3-node structure/color checks. The RR case is the
  exact shape that exposed the mirror-Case-3 bug during review, so it's a
  direct regression test for that fix.

This was drafted in full in the prior turn and diffed against the current
file; the diff below is exactly that draft, applied as a sequence of
separate edits so each can be approved individually.

**Known blocker, out of scope for this change:** `rb_foreach` at
`src/rbtree.c:204-212` is still a stub. Several existing cases (7-13) and
the moved-in cases already depend on it, and will fail/abort at that
`assert` until it's implemented. Not drafting or implementing `rb_foreach`
here per explicit instruction -- this plan only touches the test file.

## Changes to tests/test_rbtree.c (as separate approvable edits)

1. Insert two new cases between the existing descending-run case (old
   Case 8) and the LR zigzag case (old Case 9):
   - **New Case 9 (LL line):** keys `{"c","b","a"}`, minimal 3-node
     straight-line left rotation at the root ("b" becomes black root, "a"
     red left child, "c" red right child). Includes white-box color/shape
     asserts, not just `rb_validate`.
   - **New Case 10 (RR line):** keys `{"a","b","c"}`, the mirror -- the
     exact shape that exposed the mirror-Case-3 bug. Same white-box asserts.

2. Renumber the "Case N" comment labels on the five blocks that follow
   (LR zigzag, RL zigzag, mixed order, duplicate-key/NULL value_free,
   key-survives-caller-free): 9→11, 10→12, 11→13, 12→14, 13→15. Comment
   text only, no logic changes.

3. Delete `test_rb_insert_bst_only` and its helper `bst_inorder_collect`,
   along with the header comment describing it as a temporary pre-fixup
   checkpoint (currently spanning roughly lines 817-948). Its degenerate
   ascending-chain sub-test is dropped entirely (contradicted by fixup).
   Its other two sub-cases move into `test_rb_insert` as:
   - **New Case 16:** the "m,f,t,d,h" multi-level-recolor shape test,
     corrected to expect `m`, `f`, `t` as `RB_BLACK` (was incorrectly
     `RB_RED`, the pre-fixup expectation), with `rb_validate(t) == 0` added,
     and using the real `rb_foreach` instead of the white-box
     `bst_inorder_collect` walk.
   - **New Case 17:** the destroy-frees-real-nodes test, unchanged except
     adding `rb_validate(t) == 0` and dropping the "bst" framing from its
     name/printf message.

4. Update `main()` to drop the now-deleted `test_rb_insert_bst_only()` call.

No changes to `src/rbtree.c` or any other file.

## Verification

- `make test` -- expected to still fail partway through (at the first
  `rb_foreach`-dependent assertion) since `rb_foreach` remains a stub; this
  is the known, called-out blocker above, not a regression from this change.
- Once `rb_foreach` is implemented in a later change, re-run `make test`,
  `make asan`, `make memcheck` per CLAUDE.md's DONE criteria.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
